title: Herdr executor D: enforce the artifact boundary with an exclude and a collect backstop
description:
The artifact boundary is ENFORCED by the executor, never requested in a prompt.

Seen live on wave 2 of this epic: the bcv and wgi workers both committed their
RESULT file onto their attempt branch. Every other worker left it untracked,
which is what teardown expects. Under the tk herd ritual nothing PREVENTS the
commit — the prompt just asks, and two of four workers ignored it.

`.tick/learnings.md` already carries the rule, from an earlier incident:

    Problem: A worker committed tracker state although its prompt forbade it.
    Rule:    A boundary the substrate can enforce must not rest on
             instruction-following — make it impossible and REPORT every
             attempt.

Phase 1's subprocess executor implements it in TWO layers, and the herdr
executor inherits the obligation but not the code:

1. PREVENT. Start writes a git exclude for the artifact prefix into the worktree
   BEFORE the runner is launched (git.go excludeFromGit), so an ordinary
   `git add -A` cannot pick the report up. Dispose removes the line FIRST, while
   the worktree it was resolved against still exists, so nothing is orphaned in
   info/exclude.
2. DETECT, because prevention is bypassable. Collect re-checks the boundary
   against the branch diff and treats a report or artifact found there as a
   violation (collect.go:83, :185-186). The subprocess fixture `force_report`
   exists precisely to drive a runner that does `git add -f` past the exclude.
   A10 requires the attempt be REPORTED, not silently refused: violations are
   recorded as observations and carried into the collected record's
   boundary_violations.

The mechanism differs here — a herdr worker's worktree is created through herdr
rather than by this executor — but the two obligations do not. Neither may
depend on the worker's prompt, its cooperation, or which agent kind is running.

Builds on tick 3gv.

acceptance_criteria: An exclude for the report/artifact prefix is written into the worktree before the agent is started, and removed on dispose while the worktree still exists; a worker doing an ordinary git add -A cannot get its report onto the branch, proven by a fixture; a worker that force-adds past the exclude IS caught at collect, refused, and reported as a boundary violation carried in the collected record rather than dropped, proven by a second fixture; neither layer depends on the prompt or the agent kind; go test -short -timeout 45m ./... green (make test-short).
closed_reason: Merged into the integration branch. gwc and p6b resolved as a union in collect.go's classify (wallExceeded and artifactViolations both kept) and the doc status list.
